matched_rules.because: The datacenter control system was in the process of failing away from one of its control hosts, which is the exact 'when' condition for treating a control-system failover as a cooling-availability event.

The control system was unavailable, operators had minimum visibility into cooling health, and cooling did not transition to safe cooling or purge mode in part of the datacenter, matching the 'when' conditions for manually working the cooling chain and resetting PLCs.
Mechanical cooling is down in a portion of the datacenter and EC2 servers have begun shutting down due to overheating, indicating the thermal buffer is depleting and automated shutdowns have started.

next_actions.action: Manually investigate the affected cooling equipment, check the PLCs controlling the air handling units, reset affected equipment and PLCs into maximum cooling configuration, and confirm cooling is restored and temperatures are falling before standing down.

Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted; expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin, and recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down.

Treat the control-system failover as a period of elevated risk to cooling availability and watch the cooling plant directly, not only the control system; expect that a fault in the control system logic during this exchange can make the control system unresponsive; verify that cooling systems have actually entered their designed maximum-cooling fallback rather than assuming the fallback engaged.

escalate.reason: Temperatures are rising and servers have begun powering off, and thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started.

not_covered: No rule addresses the failure of purge mode itself as a distinct event; R-004 covers manual recovery but does not explicitly treat purge failure as a separate signal.
No rule addresses the specific impact on customer workloads beyond the general guardrail G-002.
No rule addresses coordination with IT service recovery or failover, which is explicitly out of scope for this pill.

per_finding.note: R-003 explicitly warns that a fault in control system logic during failover can make the control system unresponsive.
R-003 directs verifying that cooling systems actually entered maximum-cooling fallback rather than assuming it engaged.
R-004 points to checking and resetting PLCs but does not identify PLC failure as the cause of purge mode not working.
R-004's condition explicitly notes control system unavailable and operators having minimum visibility into cooling health.
R-004's next action is to manually investigate, reset affected equipment and PLCs, and put them into maximum cooling configuration.
No rule or action addresses disabling the failover mode that triggered the bug.
R-004 directs manual reset but does not mention training local operations teams to quickly identify and remediate the situation.
No rule or action addresses modifying air handling unit control to let purge mode bypass PLC controllers.
R-002 warns of hardware damage from rapid temperature rise but does not address longer recovery or instance retirement.
